title: Thirsting for God in a Dry Land
speaker: Jonathan Baird
summary: We can be dry and weary as Christians. The answer is to run hard after Christ, and David's longing in the wilderness was for the house of God.
exhortation: We can be dry and weary spiritually as Christians and find ourselves in a spiritual desert. The answer is to run earnestly after Christ, seeking the fellowship of Jesus with all our heart. What a wonderful psalm, reminding us that in our dryness and weariness we can find comfort, encouragement and power in the house of the Lord.

Notice what David says: "So I have looked upon you in the sanctuary." When he is dry and weary, he longs for the house of God. Do you long for church? Do you find comfort, peace and rest there? David did. Don't ever be fooled into thinking you can do this on your own, apart from the people of God. In church we are reminded of the gospel and the great love Jesus shows us in his life, death and resurrection. In church we have sweet fellowship with other faithful Christians, and in church we are refreshed in the presence of God.

So as we head into another weekend, whether you're dry and weary or excited and feeling good, let's be excited about what God is going to do at church this Sunday. Let's prepare our hearts to receive the word, ask God to open our eyes to those around us who are dry and weary and need lifting up, and believe in faith that God will move in and through us.
prayer: Lord, whom have I in heaven but you? And there is nothing on earth I desire besides you. There is none like you, Lord Jesus. Fill us with your Spirit to defeat every work of the enemy today, all the raging of the flesh that would lead us back down the path of addiction and sin, and every lie that there is any path to true happiness apart from Christ. From that very first fruit until today, it has been a lie that there is any true joy apart from you.

May we look to your finished work on the cross, to your blood poured out, and to the great lengths you went to so that we could return to you. Help us run to you today, where new mercies are waiting. In Jesus' name, amen.
